strategy_summary: Result: 102 wins, 103 losses, 95 ties, effectively even. The AI's top guess matched my move in 101 of 293 model rounds (34%). When it was at least 90% confident (80 rounds) it was right 26 times.

Rounds 8-30 (4-10-9): I reasoned from my own habits and picked the move that was safe against its two likeliest guesses. That reasoning is itself a pattern, and without the percentages I could not see its state. It guessed my move in 10 of 23 (43%) of these rounds.

Rounds 31-82 (18-22-12): I switched to a source it cannot learn, the digits of pi (3,6,9 rock; 1,4,7 paper; 2,5,8 scissors; 0 skipped), with a few overrides that mostly failed. Random play cannot be out-predicted on average; this stretch was unlucky (it matched 22 of 52 (42%)), helped by chance runs in the digits.

Rounds 92-160 (28-18-23): the triple rule. I looked up the last time my previous three moves had occurred and played the move that beats the counter to what I played then. The model tends to guess that I will repeat what I did last time in the same spot, and it cannot see beyond six moves. This won clearly for about 50 rounds, then the model adapted (3-9-4 in rounds 145-160).

Rounds 161-224 (21-22-21): I tried to out-adapt it with level-two versions of the rule, a lag-one read and a relation table. Each new idea won for a few rounds and then lost; overall about even. A recount showed the plain rule would have done better than my variants over rounds 180-224.
Rounds 225-300 (24-25-27): I held the plain triple rule to the end. It was ahead by five at round 255, then lost the lead in two bad patches (258-263 and 283-290).

Conclusion: blind, I found no durable edge. A fresh rule beats the model for roughly 30-50 rounds, because it needs that long to learn the rule; after that it predicts the rule's output. With the hints visible (30-12-28 over 70 rounds) I could see its confidence and stay one step ahead; without them the match is a coin flip.

Setup note: played with play_attention.js in blind mode. I used the status command (plain move history, no probabilities) during play. Per-round reasons were logged as I went and are included in the rounds below. One user question arrived mid-match (round 82) and did not change any information available to me.
